# Results — Study 848 ("Costco Hot-Dog Index")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The $1.50 hot-dog-and-soda
combo has been nominally frozen since ~1985, a folk "anti-inflation" icon. We test the two
things the narrative smuggles together: (a) the combo's **real** price has collapsed with
CPI — a mechanical identity we quantify — and (b) whether Costco's (`COST`) pricing-power /
membership model gives its **stock** a distinctive edge that lets it outrun CPI and SPY,
in particular a beta to **inflation surprises** that differs from consumer staples (`XLP`).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

*Run stamp — as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete calendar month; no partial-month bar); COST/SPY/CPI Fingerprint `cbd3b6799d57`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance month-end total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`) — **COST**, **SPY**, **XLP** (consumer-staples control); cached under `_cache/` |
| CPI | **Real** monthly `CPIAUCSL` (CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average, SA, 1982-84=100 = BLS `CUSR0000SA0`), 2000-01 → 2026-06, **fetched from the BLS public API and cached** — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). 1985 anchor `CPI_1985 = 107.6` (CPIAUCSL 1985 annual average). One point (2025-10) interpolated — the SA suspension |
| Combo | `$1.50` hot-dog + 20oz soda, nominally unchanged since ~1985 (public record) |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 (month-end; no partial-month bar) |
| Panel | **318** months (2000-01 → 2026-06), inner-joined COST×SPY×XLP×CPI |
| Signal | inflation **surprise** = ΔYoY inflation (month-on-month change in the trailing-12-month CPI inflation rate — the "inflation accelerating?" innovation) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: surprise known at close of month `t` → the timer holds `t → t+1`; one-way cost × NAV per switch |
| Fingerprint | `[cost, spy, cpi]` → **`cbd3b6799d57`** (`hotdog_index.data.fingerprint`) |

> **Data provenance, stated plainly.** CPI is the **real** FRED/BLS `CPIAUCSL` series
> (`CUSR0000SA0`), pulled from the BLS public API in ≤10-year chunks and cached. FRED's own
> `fredgraph.csv` endpoint is unreachable from this build host, so BLS is the primary feed;
> the same real public-record values are embedded in `data.py` as an offline fallback so the
> machinery tests never touch the network. Its multi-decade *level path* (169.3 in 2000-01 →
> 332.6 in 2026-06, +96%) and *2021-23 surge* (YoY peaked **+9.0%** in 2022-06) are the
> load-bearing facts. COST/SPY/XLP are the **real** equity tape (yfinance). Survivorship is
> named on the Signal axis: COST is a *hindsight-selected* single name (we know it did well —
> that is why it is famous for the hot dog), so its win is descriptive, never a forward
> promise.

## Half 1 — the folk icon is literally true: the real price has collapsed (an identity)

The combo is nominally `$1.50` every year; its purchasing-power cost in **1985 dollars** is
`$1.50 · CPI_1985 / CPI_t`. This is arithmetic, not a t-test — CPI only sets the magnitude.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| price level since 1985 (CPI multiple) | **3.09×** |
| real price of the combo today, in 1985 dollars | **$0.49** |
| **real value eroded** | **−67.6%** |
| price that would preserve 1985 real value | **$4.64** |
| per-combo "giveaway" vs 1985 pricing | **$3.14** |

The $1.50 combo really has shed **two-thirds** of its real value; to hold its 1985
purchasing power it would sell for **$4.64** today. Costco is effectively subsidising
**~$3.14** of real value per combo relative to 1985. **The erosion is real — and completely
mechanical.** It says nothing about the stock.

## Half 2 — the total-return race: COST vs CPI vs SPY (2000-2026, 26.5 yrs)

Total-return levels; CPI as a pure deflator. `$10,000` invested at the 2000-01 month-end:

| asset | growth multiple | CAGR | real (CPI-deflated) multiple | $10,000 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **COST** (total return) | **28.7×** | **+13.5%** | **14.6×** | **$286,935** |
| SPY | 8.5× | +8.4% | 4.3× | $85,393 |
| CPI (the deflator) | 2.0× | +2.6% | 1.0× | $19,644 |

COST did outrun both the market and inflation — massively (a **14.6×** real multiple). But
that is a **descriptive, hindsight-selected fact** about one exceptional mega-cap, not
evidence of an *inflation-hedge mechanism*. Even COST's monthly *excess* return over SPY
(+0.38%/mo) carries only Newey-West *t* = **1.37** (early era 0.87, late 1.11) — it does not
clear the |t| ≥ 2 bar and is not robust across eras. "COST went up a lot" and "COST hedges
inflation" are different claims; only the second is tradable, and only the second is Half 3.

## Half 3 — the signal: is COST a distinctive inflation hedge? (Newey-West, 6-lag)

Regress each asset's monthly return on the inflation surprise (ΔYoY). The claim predicts
COST should carry a positive inflation beta that **beats a boring staples basket**.

| regression | slope (inflation β) | HAC *t* | R² | tradable? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| **COST ~ surprise (same month)** | **+0.115** | **+0.13** | 0.01% | the inflation β — **≈ zero** |
| SPY ~ surprise | +0.879 | +1.27 | 0.83% | (market) |
| XLP ~ surprise (staples) | +0.302 | +0.72 | 0.16% | (staples control) |
| COST ~ surprise, **next month** | +0.652 | +0.89 | 0.26% | predictive — nothing |
| **COST − XLP gap** (β_COST − β_staples) | **−0.186** | **−0.27** | — | **no distinctive edge** |
| COST − SPY gap | −0.764 | −1.45 | — | none |

COST's inflation-surprise beta is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** (*t* =
+0.13), *smaller* than both the market's and a plain staples basket's, and the COST-minus-
staples gap is **negative and insignificant** (*t* = −0.27) — the exact opposite of "pricing
power gives it a special inflation edge." No cell clears |t| = 2 in any direction: the
*predictive* COST−staples and COST−SPY gaps are the strongest at only *t* = +1.43 / +1.75,
and the placebo below buries even those.

## Half 4 — the placebo & sub-era cut

Block-rotate the surprise against COST's return (6-month blocks, 3,000 draws); split the
sample at 2013.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed COST inflation-β slope | **+0.115** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.04 (0.72) |
| two-sided placebo *p* | **0.88** |
| early era (2000–2012) COST β *t* | **−0.05** |
| late era (2013–2026) COST β *t* | **+0.36** |

COST's inflation beta sits **squarely inside** its placebo band (*p* = 0.88) and is a flat
nothing in **both** halves of the sample (early *t* = −0.05, late *t* = +0.36). There is no
era in which the "hot-dog pricing-power inflation hedge" shows up in the tape.

## Half 5 — the money test: an inflation-timing overlay, net of costs

Hold COST when the inflation surprise known at `t−1` is positive (inflation accelerating),
cash at 2%/yr otherwise; 10 bp one-way per switch (4.1 switches/yr, invested 49% of months).
Sharpe is **excess of cash**.

| strategy | Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| inflation-timing overlay on COST (net 10bp) | **0.34** |
| buy & hold COST | **0.46** |
| SPY | **0.40** |

The overlay **underperforms simply buy-and-holding COST** (0.34 vs 0.46): timing on the
inflation surprise *destroys* return, because the signal forecasts nothing (Half 3) and you
sit in cash through half of COST's compounding. Buy-hold COST beats SPY here (0.46 vs 0.40),
but only because COST is a phenomenal *hindsight-selected* stock (and even that edge is
*t* = 1.37, not robust), not because inflation timing added anything. You shouldered
single-name, one-commodity-icon concentration for a signal that does negative work. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly world where `cost_ret = edge·surprise + noise` (SPY/XLP do not
load on the surprise). 20 seeds:

| world | COST inflation-β slope | HAC *t* | COST−XLP gap *t* | fires (\|t\|≥2) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | −0.28 | **−0.24** | −0.28 | **1/20** |
| planted (`edge = 8`), **20 seeds** | +7.72 | **+7.02** | +6.05 | **20/20** |

The detector recovers a *planted* inflation beta cleanly (and lights up the COST-vs-staples
gap) yet never fires on the null — so the real-tape `NONE` is a *true* null, not a broken
pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** COST's contemporaneous inflation-surprise beta is *t* = **+0.13**
  (≈ zero), it is **not** distinguishable from a boring staples basket (COST−XLP gap
  *t* = **−0.27**), the placebo *p* = **0.88**, and it is a flat nothing in both sub-eras
  (early *t* = −0.05, late *t* = +0.36). The "pricing power outruns inflation" story has **no
  inflation beta behind it** — COST is a growth/quality stock, not an inflation hedge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The inflation-timing overlay **loses** to buy-and-hold COST
  (Sharpe 0.34 vs 0.46) — the "hedge" signal actively hurts. COST beating SPY (0.46 vs 0.40)
  is a *hindsight-selected* mega-cap whose own monthly excess return over SPY is only
  *t* = 1.37 — survivorship, not a repeatable inflation edge.
- **Real-price erosion — CONFIRMED (mechanical).** The folk icon's *factual* core is true:
  the $1.50 combo has lost **67.6%** of its real value since 1985 (it would cost **$4.64**
  to hold 1985 purchasing power). But that is an **arithmetic identity** of a frozen nominal
  price under CPI — a great story about *Costco's marketing*, not a signal in *its stock*.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** CPI here is the **real** FRED/BLS `CPIAUCSL` series
> (`CUSR0000SA0`), fetched from the BLS public API and cached; the single 2025-10 point is
> interpolated (the SA suspension). COST/SPY/XLP are real month-end total-return tape. The
> inflation-surprise beta is ~zero and inside its placebo, and COST's real win is a
> **survivorship-selected** single name — informative history, not a forward promise.
